title: Deploy ASP.NET Core to Elastic Beanstalk
description: Create an Elastic Beanstalk environment and deploy an ASP.NET Core app using Visual Studio and the AWS CLI.

data.text: You can deploy ASP.NET Core to Elastic Beanstalk directly from Visual Studio, through the AWS CLI, or with a CI/CD pipeline. This lesson shows the first two approaches.
Publish your ASP.NET Core app as a framework-dependent or self-contained deployment. Elastic Beanstalk expects a ZIP file containing the published output.

data.title: Publish the ASP.NET Core app
data.content: Use the dotnet CLI to publish the app for release.

items: Right-click the ASP.NET Core project and choose **Publish**
Choose an existing environment or create a new one
Select the instance type and environment tier

data.title: Create an Elastic Beanstalk application and environment
data.content: Use the AWS CLI to create the application and deploy the ZIP file.
data.code:
# Create the application
aws elasticbeanstalk create-application --application-name aspnet-aws-app

# Create the environment
aws elasticbeanstalk create-environment --application-name aspnet-aws-app --environment-name aspnet-aws-env --solution-stack-name '64bit Windows Server 2019 v2.7.0 running IIS 10.0' --option-settings file://options.json

# Upload and deploy the application version
aws elasticbeanstalk create-application-version --application-name aspnet-aws-app --version-label v1 --source-bundle S3Bucket=my-bucket,S3Key=app.zip
aws elasticbeanstalk update-environment --environment-name aspnet-aws-env --version-label v1

data.title: Deploy a sample API
data.description: Publish a minimal API to Elastic Beanstalk and verify the response.
steps: Create a minimal API with `dotnet new web -n WeatherApi`
Add a GET `/weather` endpoint returning a JSON forecast
Deploy with Visual Studio Publish or AWS CLI
Browse to the Elastic Beanstalk environment URL
data.expectedOutcome: You see the weather JSON response served from Elastic Beanstalk.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use Visual Studio Publish for manual deployments
Use AWS CLI for scripted deployments
Elastic Beanstalk runs the published output without IIS management
Store configuration in environment variables, not in code
data.takeaway: Deployment is the moment your local ASP.NET Core app becomes a live AWS endpoint.
